For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). \[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,

\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.

The replacement makes the intended fixed-mixture subclass and every division and moment condition explicit; it does not assume the proposition's annihilation or risk conclusion.

The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!6^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +4(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[

\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le

   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}

holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\

    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}

\[

 \right\},

There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, or uniform inference result.

The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs.  Select and fix the one once-for-all witness bank whose existence is asserted in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) using \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).  Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad fixed-separated non-Gaussian class has the existence-level fixed-bank rate
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Conditional on that selected bank, the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\); no effective construction of the bank is asserted.  Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.  The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here.  These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

{"id":"def:adaptive-contour-estimator","name":"Certified split-sample statistic on the translated-dyadic bank","construction":"Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).","free_symbols":["Fhat","Ghat","I0","I1","Cj","aStar","Nhat","jhat","J","rho","thetahatSpec","Ctheta","n","Y","Z","bargn","eta"],"inputs":["def:contour-bank-handle","I0","I1","Fhat","Ghat"]}

{"id":"def:adaptive-contour-estimator","name":"Canonical certified split-sample statistic on the translated-dyadic bank","construction":"Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  Termination, extensionality, and Borel measurability of this canonical algorithm are conclusions proved in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\), not assumptions of the definition.","free_symbols":["O","n","i","X","T","Y","bargn","Z","I0","I1","Fhat","Ghat","k","delta","psieta","R0","R1","Cj","rho","J","aStar","Nhat","jhat","Ctheta","thetahatSpec","eta"],"inputs":["O","bargn","n","Ctheta","k","delta","psieta","R0","R1"]}

There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, or uniform inference result.

changed.from: If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.
changed.to:
If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants. Moreover, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\), the same construction may be started from any \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and preserves its law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the noise \(\eta\), both clipped supplied codes, and therefore the two bounds
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
Every law on this second path belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), has target \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\), and obeys the same product relative-entropy bound. Consequently there is \(c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge \frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}.
\]
changed.reason: The current lemma records only the broad-class branch. The same outcome tilt preserves the published ACE class because it leaves the entire treatment law, both regression functions, both clipped codes, and both \(L^r(P_X)\) code errors unchanged; adding this branch exposes the transferable two-point converse required by the maximality directive.

\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]

The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[

\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). \[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]

 =\frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
        {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}

\[
 \bigl||a|-\rho_j\bigr|\ge h_{\star}
\]
for every zero \(a\) strictly inside \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\).  This circle encloses the zero localized in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), so \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\).

\[

\]

\[

 \ge \frac{|z-a_\nu|}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+|z|}
 \ge \frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}.
\]
The last base lies in \((0,1)\), and \(N\le N_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Multiplying this bound and using (3) yields
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|
 \ge
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}
 =a_{\mathrm{an}}
 \ge a_{\star}>0. \tag{4}
\]

These operations use only the displayed primitive constants and never the unknown transform or law of \(\eta\). \[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). If a concrete implementation satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is added and compiled, then, relative to the canonical floor-dyadic observation records and exactly the same fixed records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), the statistic is also the value of a total executable represented-data transducer returning a certified-real name. The correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records. Identical full input records, including their primitive components, give identical traces and output records; no Type-2 computability or trace extensionality across arbitrary alternative real names is asserted.  Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.

\[

 \le

 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and

No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. {"id":"thm:common-experiment-dichotomy","kind":"theorem","statement":"The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Also fix once for all the exact primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) specified in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Under this shared-record convention, apply and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate specified by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total Borel statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Its ordinary-sample interpretation canonicalizes only observation-coordinate records and uses the same fixed primitive records. If the bounded-build substrate in \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is concretely implemented and compiled, the statistic is additionally delivered by the represented-data transducer on the identical fixed primitive records and supplied canonical observation records. Its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records, and trace determinism is asserted only for identical full input records. No computability claim from arbitrary alternative real names is made. Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.","free_symbols":["gcode","qcode","bargn","barqn","n","eps1n","eps2n","eps0","PNG","RNG","thetahatSpec","P","PG","theta0","RG","MGquant","gamma"],"depends_on":["def:non-gaussian-class","def:gaussian-class","def:minimax-risks","def:adaptive-contour-estimator","thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax","prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy","lem:finite-contour-bank"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"The theorem records the fixed-separated non-Gaussian rate and the Gaussian zero-target diagnostic as separate facts on separately defined classes.","gap":"The incomparable classes do not determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier.","consumer":"Do not describe the paired display as a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy."}

{"id":"def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate","name":"Paper-independent bounded-build certified complex contour arithmetic substrate","construction":"The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification.  A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
 x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
 \qquad
 I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) with \(p\le x\).  Executable code may inspect only the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It may not inspect a semantic exact-real value.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
 A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
 \qquad
 A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
\[
 A B=
 [\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
  \max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\).  Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
 (A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), put
\[
 \operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
 \min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Thus \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds.  Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures: after \(q\) bisections their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\).  This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds.  Division is the guarded operation
\[
 \frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
 =(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
and is executed only when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed, rather than postulated, from Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
 \arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
 \qquad
 |R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures.  If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), so this is an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations.  The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
 3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
 N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\).  Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested.  Hence
\[
 \exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle.  Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
 r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive.  If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell.  Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations therefore yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures.  Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations.  Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) only if it implements these algorithms, exports their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiles the resulting module.  This definition is the explicit bounded-build obligation; it does not state or imply that the missing complex operations are already exported by Causalean.  Until such an implementation is added and compiled, later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.","free_symbols":[],"inputs":[]}

{"id":"def:contour-bank-handle","name":"Certified translated-dyadic contour bank","construction":"The certified-real convention is the following.  The integer \(k\) is given exactly, and each of the positive reals \(\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\) is supplied by its canonical nested dyadic enclosure name.  No transform, distribution, oracle, or sample-dependent object is an input.  Put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
Refine outward intervals until the positive denominator in \(Q_{\star}\) has a positive rational lower endpoint and \(Q_{\star}\) has a finite rational upper endpoint \(U_{\star}\), and set \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}=\lceil U_{\star}\rceil\).  For \(m\ge3\), define
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Refine an outward interval for \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\) until its rational lower endpoint \(L_{\star}\) is positive.  Let \(u_{\star}\ge1\) be the least integer with \(2^{-u_{\star}}\le L_{\star}\), and set \(a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}\).  Set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).  This is the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank.  Its construction inputs are exactly the certified primitive constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); the unknown law of \(\eta\) is not an input.  The universal guarantee for treatment-noise transforms is stated and proved separately in \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).","free_symbols":["k","delta","psieta","R0","R1","rho","J","aStar","Cj","eta"],"inputs":["k","delta","psieta","R0","R1"]}

{"id":"def:contour-bank-handle","name":"Certified translated-dyadic contour bank","construction":"Let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote an actually supplied positive certified-real record satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  As part of the experiment convention, fix once for all the single actual record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1),
\]
with the value contracts
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Each positive name includes its rational positivity witness.  The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the only primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator.  The construction reads only its supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It never reconstructs a name from an exact real and does not quantify over alternative records representing the same constants.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one.  If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), put
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is \(\rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\).  Enumerate these radii increasingly and set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
